Agent: a shared `research` agent from the family file: a fresh sandbox per conversation, memory search off, no accounts, `web_search` and `web_fetch` only, its own capped key. Each parent's agent gains `sessions_spawn` with `subagents.allowAgents: ["research"]` and `runTimeoutSeconds`. Guardrails: both `dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` keys unset, `tools.web.fetch.headers` empty, no fetch-provider plugin, `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy` off, `browser.enabled: false`, `browser.evaluateEnabled: false`. One rule in the helper's AGENTS.md: give the link and the time fetched, show the page's own date when it has one, give a price or date only from a fetched page, say 'could not verify'. In each parent's AGENTS.md the 'cannot open links' line becomes the hand-off rule, with what a task may carry; its smoke-eval case changes too. Four planted eval cases. Tony's agent first, Jordan's a day later. No plugin; no house-rules rule.
depends_on: The outbound gate, built first in the same plan (Tony's answer 7b; the roadmap's gate before web reading): the firewall blocking every program by default with one rule per program, and the outbound proxy for the gateway's calls enforcing after at least one night in report mode; the plugin allowlist left open at the M1 sign-off is closed in the same step. No other card carries this work, so its hours are counted on this card
T4 passes first: a hand-off from a parent's agent returns the helper's answer with agent-to-agent messaging off and session visibility set to self (the roadmap lists this as not yet confirmed)

Four planted eval cases pass before go-live: a home-network address, a public address that redirects to one, a public name that resolves to one, and a result that asks the parent's agent to pass its notes to the helper
If the mail lookup (G015) is live: its seeded-mail test is run again with the helper present
Tony provides a new capped model key for the helper at execution
caveats: The plain fetch runs no JavaScript and cannot log in, so such pages stay unread until the extra readers (F020) exist, and Happy says 'could not verify'. A slow lookup gets no 'on it' and no plain-words 'cancel that': the helper's built-in finish report is the only progress message, and a lookup ends at its time limit or at Tony's built-in stop.

If the hand-off test (T4) fails, the only documented alternative is session visibility `tree` for the whole gateway, which changes a signed-off setting and needs Tony's yes plus a re-run of the separation check.

The home-network block rests on the fetch tool resolving and pinning the address itself, so `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy` stays off and both private-network keys stay truly unset: an explicitly written `false` on the browser key turns hostname navigation into an allowlist and would stop the later research browser (F020).

Once the helper can fetch pages, neither the firewall nor the proxy can hold the gateway program to a list of hosts; they refuse home-network addresses and nothing more, so tool permissions, not the firewall, keep the other agents off the web.

The answer rule and the rule on what goes into a task (the town and the children's ages yes, names and the school no) are prompt rules; nothing mechanical enforces them, and the planted eval cases are the only check. The roadmap's prompt-injection tripwire is not built with this card: by Tony's answer of 12 Oct it waits for local models.

The fetch tool's home-network check covers `web_fetch` only, so host-side helpers that take a web address (the summarize wrapper, the print download, watcher scripts) need their own scheme, host and resolved-address checks.
edits.safety: The helper reads untrusted pages but holds no memory, accounts or family data, and cannot reach the home network. The roadmap's one remaining leak path stays open: a parent's agent holds private chats and writes the task text for a helper that can fetch any public address. A prompt rule and planted tests guard it; the helper's answer is treated as untrusted.
unverified: That a cross-agent hand-off returns its result with agent-to-agent messaging off and session visibility set to self: the roadmap lists this as untested on 2026.9.7, and nothing was run here (T4).
The rule on what may go into the task text is a prompt rule; nothing mechanical enforces what a parent's agent writes into it.
Nothing in the installed stack enforces citations; it is a prompt rule the model can ignore, and the eval cases are the only check.
Whether page fetches pass through the outbound proxy once it is configured: the installed docs point both ways and nothing has been tried; it is read from the proxy's log when the gate is built.
The explicit-false behaviour of the browser policy was read in the installed source only; the docs do not describe it and it was not exercised.
How long a real lookup takes: nothing on the current stack runs longer than about 20 seconds, so whether an 'on it' line is ever needed is unknown until the hand-off exists.

Then an in-house host-side tool plugin wrapping `remindctl` with three verbs (list, add, complete) on that one list only, no delete and no due dates, allowed on both parents' own agents in the agent's tool list and the sandbox's. Reminders access is granted once by hand in the gateway's own process context. One instruction: when 'remind me' could mean a timed text or a list item, ask.
